name: SENsation
cuisine: Cantonese with Sichuan dishes (modern Chinese neo-bistro)
opened: late 2024 / early 2025 (Time Out lists it among '10 tables ouvertes en 2025'; Sortiraparis 'new' review updated Feb 2025; Michelin tags it 'Nouveau')
price: Set menu EUR 58 (5 courses); a la carte EUR 30-57; Peking duck EUR 68 half / 130 whole (Le Fooding)
halal_note: No halal claim found; menu includes pork (siu mai).
summary: Chef Samuel Lee (Hong Kong-born, about 10 years at Shang Palace, where he earned its Michelin star) opened his own place. Classic Cantonese dishes such as siu mai and roast duck, plus Sichuan classics.

name: Feel Ling - La Table
cuisine: Cantonese bistro (Asian canteen at lunch, Cantonese at dinner)
opened: 2026 (restaurant site: 'notre second restaurant vient d'ouvrir'; Time Out review published 17 June 2026)
price: Starters EUR 8-12, mains about EUR 25 (Time Out); Time Out price level 2/4
summary: Second, more refined site of the Feel Ling canteen (24 rue Lauriston), run by chef Sophie Ya. Time Out says it 'déclare sa flamme à la cuisine cantonaise'.

name: Fat Belly
cuisine: Asian rotisserie: Cantonese-style roast duck and roast pork, with Southeast Asian influences
region: Cantonese-style roast meats (siu mei) mixed with Southeast Asian
opened: mid-2026 (LesRestos: opening announced for June 2026, reported open July 2026; Do It In Paris article dated 10 May 2026 calls it new)
price: Weekday lunch: Cantonese roast duck EUR 21, roast pork EUR 19; wontons EUR 11-14
summary: From Norman Kolton (Street Bangkok) and Chinese-born restaurateur Sandra Tcheng. Café, restaurant and rotisserie. Sortiraparis picked it as one of two must-try new restaurants for October 2026. It is a hybrid, not purely Cantonese.

name: Dimdan Maidan
opened: by July 2025 at the latest (Sortiraparis review updated 25 July 2025); exact date not found
price: Dishes about EUR 4-16 (e.g. honey char siu rice EUR 14.50, lo mien with wontons EUR 16)
summary: Small cha chaan teng run by a Hong Kong couple. The chef previously worked at Buddha Bar and Shangri-La. Menu has curry fish balls, bolo buns, wontons, lo mien, egg tarts and yuen yeung, in 1970s-80s Hong Kong decor.

name: Wukong The Grand Master
region: Hong Kong-inspired (per Paris Zigzag); décor described as a 'Shanghai fantasmé' (Le Bonbon)
opened: around late 2024 / early 2025 (Paris Zigzag page modified 13 Jan 2025 calls it a 'nouvel établissement'; Le Bonbon 26 Mar 2025 calls it 'nouveau resto')
price: EUR EUR; discovery platter EUR 50 for two; cocktails EUR 14
halal_note: Pork siu mai on the menu.
summary: Canal Saint-Martin restaurant-bar with Wong Kar-wai / 1980s China film-set decor. Serves handmade dim sum (shrimp wontons, grilled chicken xiao long bao, pork siu mai). Regional attribution is mixed, so treat it as only loosely southern.

name: L'Oisillon
region: Hong Kong and Inner Mongolia inspirations (only partly southern)
opened: likely 2026 (Le Fooding review first published 22 Sept 2026); exact opening date not found
price: Lunch set EUR 38 (4 courses); plates EUR 12-25; Le Fooding range EUR 36-50
summary: Le Fooding lists it under Chinois/Asiatique, with dishes inspired by Inner Mongolia and Hong Kong (e.g. lamb and leek shao mai). It is only partly southern.

name: Red Katz
cuisine: Contemporary Chinese: Cantonese and Shanghainese, with dim sum
summary: Large, glamorous retro-styled Chinese restaurant in the Sentier, covered by Time Out, Sortiraparis, Paris Zigzag (which calls it Cantonese and Shanghainese) and Yonder (Oct 2024). It is borderline 'new' (late 2024).

name: La Maison Mongkok
cuisine: Hong Kong-style Cantonese with French inspiration
price: Lunch menus EUR 21.80 / 26.80; chef's 7-course menu EUR 58.80; discovery menu EUR 68.80
summary: Upscale Cantonese restaurant with a team led by Chef Long, which Sortiraparis describes as Michelin-starred. It opened mid-2024, so it falls outside the 2025-26 window and is included only as borderline.

name: 强记港式茶餐厅 (Qiangji Hong Kong-style cha chaan teng)
cuisine: Hong Kong cha chaan teng: cheung fun, bean-curd rolls, congee, siu mei rice, baked rice, HK milk tea
halal_note: Siu mei and pork congee on the menu.
summary: Chinese-language blog Playinparis calls it a recently opened ('刚开业没多久'), buzzy cha chaan teng in Chinatown. The chef is from Hong Kong and previously ran an older Cantonese restaurant in Paris. The French trading name was not confirmed, and a directory lists 'Le Palais de Choisy' at the same address, so it should be checked.

name: Zou Kee Express
opened: announced for 15 June 2026 (restaurant's own website, per search snippet); actual opening not confirmed
summary: The restaurant's own site calls it a 'Restaurant Hongkongais à Paris 13e'. The address and the June 2026 opening date come only from a search snippet of that site. No press coverage was found.

name: Fuchill
cuisine: Cantonese: dim sum, Cantonese claypots, wok dishes, noodles
price: Shrimp dumplings EUR 6.80; dan dan noodles EUR 13.80; curry chicken claypot EUR 14.80
summary: Opposite the Palais Brongniart. The site says it is 100% homemade and shows a 'Distinction 2026' label. An OpenTable review from Sept 2026 shows it was operating then. No opening date or press coverage was found, so it may not be new.

name: Lily Wang
cuisine: Chinese/Asian with Cantonese dim sum (har gow, siu mai; 6-piece assortment EUR 28)
region: Mixed Chinese (Cantonese dim sum on the menu)
opened: relaunched 2026: taken over in June 2026 by Xavier Niel, Pierre-Antoine Capton and Laurent de Gourcuff (LesRestos; Pure People 9 July 2026). The restaurant itself is older.
price: A la carte about EUR 50-70; menus EUR 29/35 (LesRestos; may predate the relaunch)
summary: A relaunch, not a new restaurant. It now has a new bar, a garden terrace and Asian cuisine by Jian Lang Wang. It is only loosely southern.

name: Saveurs de Hunan (寻湘记)
opened: establishment created 27 March 2024 (legal notices, via search snippet)
summary: Hunanese restaurant (flagged as south-central). It dates from 2024, so it is borderline for the 2025-26 window. No press review was found.

name: Le Dragon Wok
halal_note: Zabihah lists it as 'Fully halal' with a certificate on file and names AVS as the certifier or meat supplier. Zabihah also shows an 'Alcohol served' tag, which conflicts with the rest of the listing. Le Bonbon (2022-23) already listed a halal Dragon Wok at this address, so it is not new.
summary: Halal Chinese/Asian restaurant described as a 'new Asian concept 100% Halal'. However, listings going back to 2022 suggest it is an established place that may have been relaunched.

name: Le 831 (Ouïghours, 火焱山)
cuisine: Uyghur / Central Asian: hand-pulled noodles, wood-fired lamb skewers, dapanji, naan
halal_note: The restaurant site says all meat is halal from a certified supplier: HQC (Halal Quality Control) certificate ES10910900571 for supplier Carsiva Meat Solutions (Portugal), valid until 15/01/2029. This certifies the meat supply, not the restaurant itself.
summary: Popular Uyghur halal restaurant (Restaurant Guru 4.8/5, about 1,500 reviews) with karaoke rooms. Open since 2020, so it is not new.

name: ÜRÜMQI (乌鲁木齐)
halal_note: Presented as 'Restaurant Ouïghour Halal' on Mapstr and its own site. No certifier named.
summary: Uyghur halal restaurant from 2023. The restaurant site (urumqi.resto-ouighour.fr) did not resolve from this environment.

name: Muqam
cuisine: Uyghur: kawap skewers, laghman noodles, samsa
price: About EUR 25 average a la carte; dishes about EUR 15-18
halal_note: Time Out describes 'brochettes halal' (beef, lamb, chicken). No certifier named, and Zabihah shows no certification.
summary: Time Out calls it one of the only representatives of Uyghur cuisine, mixing Chinese and Turkic flavours. It is established, not new. It appears in Time Out's halal guide (page dated 23 Sept 2026).

name: Nouilles Ceintures
halal_note: Time Out describes the toppings (braised beef, shredded chicken) as 'garniture halal'. No certifier named.
summary: Small noodle counter listed in Time Out's halal guide. No opening date was found.

name: Sweetalk - TaklaMakan (塔克拉玛干新疆餐厅)
cuisine: Uyghur / Central Asian restaurant and tea salon: laghman, samsa, wonton, baklava
price: Dishes EUR 10-20; TheFork average about EUR 19
halal_note: The restaurant's page lists 'Plats halal'. No certifier named.
summary: Uyghur restaurant and tea room in the 15th, rated 9.6/10 on TheFork. No opening date was found.
